record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Bifurcation branches for the critical equation
record.original_question: For the same unit-ball problem -Δu = u^5 + λu in Ω ⊂ R^3 with zero Dirichlet boundary condition, sign-changing solution branches are known to emanate from eigenvalues associated with nonradial sign-changing eigenfunctions when λ ≥ λ1. Do any such branches reach the interval 0 < λ < λ1/4, or must they instead have vertical asymptotes at values λ ≥ λ1/4?

evidence.quote: When λ ≥ λ1 there exist sign-changing solutions of (1.1) - but no solution u > 0 of (1.1), (see [Co]). In the bifurcation diagram, branches of solutions emanate from the eigenvalues associated with non-radial sign-changing eigenfunctions. It would be interesting to decide whether such branches “reach” the interval (0, λ1/4); they might instead admit e.g. vertical asymptotes at values of λ ≥ λ1/4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^3:|x|<1\}$ be the open unit ball, and consider the Brezis–Nirenberg-type problem with critical Sobolev exponent
$$
\begin{cases} -\Delta u = u^5 + \lambda u & \text{in } \Omega,\\ u=0 & \text{on } \partial\Omega, \end{cases}
\qquad (*)
$$
where $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$ is a parameter. Let $0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2<\lambda_3<\cdots$ denote the Dirichlet eigenvalues of $-\Delta$ on $\Omega$, with associated eigenspaces $E_k$. It is known that for $\lambda\geq\lambda_1$ there exist sign-changing solutions of $(*)$ (and no positive solution), and that in the bifurcation diagram (with horizontal axis $\lambda$ and vertical axis some norm of $u$) continua of sign-changing solutions of $(*)$ emanate from those eigenvalues $\lambda_k$ ($k\geq 2$) whose eigenspace $E_k$ contains a non-radial sign-changing eigenfunction.
 
Determine whether any such bifurcation branch of sign-changing solutions can extend into the parameter interval $0<\lambda<\lambda_1/4$, or whether instead every such branch must remain confined to $\lambda\geq\lambda_1/4$ (for instance by possessing a vertical asymptote at some value $\lambda\geq\lambda_1/4$).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (including a 2025 preprint claiming a complete resolution of Brezis' first open problem) establishes existence of infinitely many sign-changing nonradial solutions of the 3D Brezis–Nirenberg equation on the ball for the full parameter range, but the specific question of whether bifurcation branches emanating from eigenvalues with nonradial sign-changing eigenfunctions actually reach the interval $(0,\lambda_1/4)$ or instead have vertical asymptotes at $\lambda\geq\lambda_1/4$ does not appear to be explicitly settled in the literature found. Status is therefore unclear.

status_evidence.title: On Brezis' First Open Problem: A Complete Solution
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence of infinitely many sign-changing nonradial solutions for the 3D Brezis–Nirenberg problem on the ball for the full range of the parameter.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of sign-changing nonradial solutions across the parameter range is now known, but this addresses existence, not the global shape of bifurcation branches from specific eigenvalues.

status_evidence.title: The Brezis–Nirenberg problem near criticality in dimension 3
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of the 3D problem indicate $\lambda^*=\lambda_1/4$ as the critical threshold below which positive solutions do not exist on the ball.
status_evidence.claim: The threshold $\lambda_1/4$ is well known but bifurcation behavior of sign-changing branches across it is not resolved in the located sources.

status_evidence.title: The second bifurcation branch for radial solutions of the Brezis-Nirenberg problem in dimension four
status_evidence.snippet: In dimension 4 the second radial bifurcation branch tends asymptotically to the first eigenvalue.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous asymptotic behavior of bifurcation branches is studied in higher dimensions, but the 3D nonradial sign-changing case remains less clear.
